newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-Chartists still await fresh dollar rally.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Chartists still await fresh dollar rally.

text.p: The dollar edged toward the upper ends of its recent ranges but failed to follow through to new multi-year highs as currency market players shunned aggressive positions ahead of several key economic events.

Technical analysts said the greenback will probably muster at least one more push past 1.6570 marks, a 31-month high, and 1.2270 yen, a four-year peak, as the global economic picture clears toward the end of this week.
"I think the dollar breaks higher. Even if we don't see the range broken this week, it's getting set up," said Ture Johnson, technical analyst at Bank of America.

The dollar climbed to the middle of its current 1.64 to 1.65 marks range Tuesday, but the bulls refused to take it the rest of the way, further delaying a run to the highs expected by many technicians.
"In the bigger picture, you've got to keep buying dollars. The weekly studies are still pretty bullish. We're just consolidating now," Johnson said.

Both dollar/mark and dollar/yen have settled into triangle patterns as the market awaits the outcomes of U.S. and British monetary policy meetings Wednesday, U.S. January jobs data Friday and a Group of Seven nations meeting Saturday.

"There's too much input this week for the market to do much trading. Triangle patterns are relatively common ahead of a series of events and numbers like this," said Dan Ascani, president and director of research at Global Market Strategists Inc.
Any fresh dollar rally will probably begin against the yen, which continues to suffer from a number of fundamental economic problems, chartists noted.
Surpassing near-term targets at 124 and 126 yen could quickly clear a path to a medium-term objective at 129, analysts said.
"People are not all that involved right now, but dollar/yen has a pretty good shot of exploding higher," Johnson said.
Mark/yen has gradually climbed to its recent range top, but needs to push past 74.50 and 74.75 before chartists will join the bull camp.
"We're at the top of the range. I favor a break higher, but it's got to break before you buy it," said Johnson.
Dealers cited the Australian dollar as a candidate for continued losses after sinking below key support at $0.77.
